Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty is a fluorine-free, water-processable binder (polyacrylic acid/carboxymethyl cellulose crosslinked by citric acid) using combined hydrogen, covalent, and ionic bonding. It matches polyvinylidene fluoride performance, improves cycle stability, enables direct recycling without fluorinated residue, and cuts energy and emissions. This offers a scalable, sustainable route to circular lithium-ion battery manufacturing.

item.title: Fast-charging and durable all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries enabled by pre-embedded solid-solid redox mediator
item.description:

Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in using an iodine-based solid-solid redox mediator pre-embedded in an amorphous sulfur/iodine nano-eutectic cathode. Iodine forms a percolating I2/I− nano-network that accelerates solid-solid sulfur redox and electron transfer. This enables fast charging (851.9 mAh g−1 at 10 C) and exceptional durability (9,000 cycles over 9 months), offering a design strategy for sluggish solid-state conversion electrodes.

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work introduces a crown ether-engineered porous liquid electrolyte that decouples catalytic activity from parasitic side reactions in aqueous zinc–sulfur batteries. By modulating Zn²⁺ solvation and sterically blocking polyiodide shuttling, it enables reversible S↔ZnS conversion, higher discharge voltage, reduced polarization, and 89% capacity retention over 1000 cycles—advancing safe, sustainable metal-chalcogen battery design.
